description: En la Luna hay más de medio millón de kilos de objetos humanos: módulos de descenso, rovers, herramientas, basura de las misiones Apollo. En Marte hay paracaídas, escudos térmicos, landers que dejaron de responder y el helicóptero Ingenuity. Están documentados en fuentes distintas y nadie los ha reunido en un solo lugar navegable.
summary:
Lunar/Mars Memory is an interactive storytelling experience built on real NASA and ESA data about the equipment humanity has abandoned on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space. It opens with a single piece of paper that seems to mean nothing until it multiplies into thousands, each one representing a real object we sent into space and never recovered: 96 on the Moon (over 187,000 kg), 15 on Mars, and probes still drifting through the solar system.

It directly addresses the “Abandoned but not Forgotten” challenge by turning NSSDCA and ESA catalog data into something people actually feel, not just read. A two-mode selector lets kids and organizations explore the same verified data at their own level.

We include a written article detailing our research and approach, along with a 30-second video that brings the story to life visually. It matters because most people have no idea how much we’ve left behind or that some of it still works.
details:
Lunar/Mars Memory turns real NASA and ESA tracking data into an interactive story about the hardware humanity has left on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space.

How it works:

The experience opens with a single piece of paper that multiplies until it fills the screen—each sheet representing an unreturned space object. Users then choose a simplified mode for kids or a technical mode for organizations to explore an interactive 3D map. Using NASA’s NSSDCA catalog and ESA debris statistics, it tracks 96 objects on the Moon (187,000+ kg), 15 on Mars (7,000+ kg), and deep-space probes like Pioneer 10.

Benefits and impact:

We shift the narrative from "space junk" to "space memory," separating waste from scientific heritage and active mysteries. Making statistics visual and emotional sparks curiosity in young audiences while giving organizations a clearer view of a growing problem.

Tools and technologies:

The serverless prototype runs on a single WebGL canvas built with React, Three.js (React Three Fiber), Spline for 3D scenes, Rive for animated UI, and local JSON files. Our 30-second demo video was generated with Remotion, tying every on-screen figure directly to NASA and ESA data.

Creativity and team considerations:

A visual metaphor one paper becoming thousands makes the scale of space debris felt rather than just read, while dual entry points engage both a ten-year-old and a policy-maker without sacrificing accuracy.
